questions.question: Which mode suits you best when you’re just getting started?

options.explanation: Correct. In Manual mode, you see every change before it’s made.
In Auto mode, Claude acts without asking. It suits you once you’re used to steering Claude.
Don’t use this mode on your own computer. Anthropic recommends it only for separate, isolated environments.

options.text: Claude investigates the project and makes a plan without changing files
options.explanation: Exactly. When the plan is good, you switch modes and Claude carries it out.

options.text: Claude makes all the changes at once without asking
options.explanation: In Plan mode, Claude doesn’t change any files. It only plans.

options.text: Claude moves the work to the cloud
options.explanation: The cloud is an environment, not a mode. Plan mode means planning before doing.

questions.question: Claude asks for your GitHub password. What do you do?

options.text: I don’t give it. Signing in is always done in the browser
options.explanation: Correct. Passwords don’t belong in the conversation.

options.text: I give it, because Claude needs it
options.explanation: Don’t give it. Claude doesn’t need passwords, and signing in is done in the browser.

options.text: I only give the first part of the password
options.explanation: Not even part of a password is given out. Signing in is always done in the browser.
